ctx.x: Yeah, so if they had some of the unissued ones there, they probably had some of the others there, too, I think. Although at one time, I know other opera collectors told me once, see, Columbia went bankrupt four or five times, I think, if that's possible, probably under different names, the American Record Corporation and all those. At one time, some of the stuff was sold out to Brunswick, and some of that stuff... When Steve Smith, I mentioned, started his record store called Hot Records Society, that was…

Yeah. Worked in Bakelite, and the hard rubber, and all that kind of junk. So... Anyway, I imagine Columbia had quite a few of the Bessies there. As late as 1939 or so. But... Oh, I was going to say, this opera collector told me, once at one period, they knew that you could go up to Bridgeport and buy any original master that you wanted to, the metal plate, for $5 was the price they'd sell. including their early opera. They had some early 1900 or 19... from 1900 to 1905 period opera on a silver label, I think it…
